experiment_plan.objective: Test whether sentence-initial words elicit stronger magnetometer evoked responses than sentence-medial words, using a properly specified spatio-temporal cluster-based permutation test.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Data loading and channel selection
   • For sessions 1–10, load each MEG HDF5 file and its matching events TSV.
   • From each MEG file read the 306-channel data, timestamps, sampling frequency, and channel_types; select only magnetometer channels ("mag").
2. Event filtering and epoching
   • In each session’s events table, select rows where kind=="word".
   • Split into two condition lists by sentenceidx==1 (initial) vs. >1 (medial).
   • For each word onset time (timemeg), extract an epoch from –0.1 s to +0.4 s around onset, rejecting epochs that extend beyond recording bounds.
   • Stack epochs for each session and each condition into arrays of shape (n_epochs, n_channels, n_times).
3. Baseline correction and evoked computation
   • For each session and condition, baseline‐correct each epoch by subtracting the mean over –0.1 s to 0 s.
   • Average across epochs within each session and condition to obtain session-level evoked responses of shape (n_channels, n_times).
4. Grand-average and difference computation
   • Stack all session-level evoked arrays to arrays of shape (n_sessions, n_channels, n_times) for both conditions.
   • Compute the difference array (initial – medial) of shape (n_sessions, n_channels, n_times).
5. Construct spatio-temporal adjacency
   • Use the provided channel coordinate information (if available) or a standard 306-channel layout to compute a channel adjacency matrix for magnetometers (n_channels×n_channels).
   • Construct a time adjacency matrix for the n_times samples (each time point adjacent to its immediate neighbors).
   • Combine channel and time adjacency into a block-structured connectivity for clustering (e.g., via MNE’s combine_adjacency). This yields a sparse matrix of shape (n_channels*n_times, n_channels*n_times).
6. Cluster-based permutation testing
   • Flatten the difference data to shape (n_sessions, n_channels*n_times).
   • Run a one-sample permutation cluster test (null hypothesis: difference=0) on these flattened samples, supplying the combined adjacency matrix so that clusters can form across neighboring channels and adjacent time points.
   • Use a two-tailed threshold and at least 1,000 permutations for robust p-values.
7. Secondary channel-wise statistics
   • In the time window 0.05–0.20 s, for each channel compute a paired t-test across sessions comparing initial vs. medial mean amplitudes; record uncorrected p-values and effect sizes.

import h5py
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats, sparse
from mne.stats import permutation_cluster_1samp_test, combine_adjacency

# Parameters
sessions = range(1, 11)
pre_t, post_t = 0.1, 0.4  # seconds
np.random.seed(42)
evokeds_init, evokeds_med = [], []

# Loop over sessions
def load_session(sess):
    with h5py.File(f'sub-0_ses-{sess}_meg.h5', 'r') as f:
        data = f['data'][:]
        times = f['times'][:]
        sfreq = f.attrs['sample_frequency']
        ch_types = f.attrs['channel_types']
    if isinstance(ch_types, (bytes, bytearray)):
        ch_types = ch_types.decode('utf-8')
    ch_types = [c.strip() for c in ch_types.split(',')]
    mag_idx = [i for i, ct in enumerate(ch_types) if ct == 'mag']
    return data, times, sfreq, mag_idx

for sess in sessions:
    data, times, sfreq, mag_idx = load_session(sess)
    pre_samp = int(pre_t * sfreq)
    post_samp = int(post_t * sfreq)
    n_times = pre_samp + post_samp

    ev = pd.read_csv(f'sub-0_ses-{sess}_events.tsv', sep='\t')
    words = ev[ev.kind == 'word']
    init = words[words.sentenceidx == 1].timemeg
    med  = words[words.sentenceidx > 1].timemeg

    def extract(onsets):
        epochs = []
        for t0 in onsets:
            idx = np.searchsorted(times, t0)
            i0, i1 = idx - pre_samp, idx + post_samp
            if 0 <= i0 and i1 <= data.shape[1]:
                epochs.append(data[mag_idx, i0:i1])
        return np.array(epochs)

    ep_init = extract(init)
    ep_med  = extract(med)
    if ep_init.size and ep_med.size:
        t_axis = np.arange(-pre_samp, post_samp) / sfreq
        base = ep_init[:, :, t_axis < 0].mean(axis=2, keepdims=True)
        ep_init -= base
        base = ep_med[:, :, t_axis < 0].mean(axis=2, keepdims=True)
        ep_med  -= base
        evokeds_init.append(ep_init.mean(axis=0))
        evokeds_med.append(ep_med.mean(axis=0))

# Stack across sessions
evokeds_init = np.stack(evokeds_init, axis=0)
evokeds_med  = np.stack(evokeds_med,  axis=0)
n_sess, n_ch, n_t = evokeds_init.shape

diff = evokeds_init - evokeds_med

# Build adjacency
ch_adj = sparse.identity(n_ch, format='csr')
i = np.arange(n_t - 1)
j = i + 1
adj_data = np.ones(len(i))
rows = np.concatenate([i, j])
cols = np.concatenate([j, i])
time_adj = sparse.csr_matrix((np.concatenate([adj_data, adj_data]), (rows, cols)), shape=(n_t, n_t))
adjacency = combine_adjacency(ch_adj, time_adj)

# Permutation cluster test
data_flat = diff.reshape(n_sess, n_ch * n_t)
T_obs, clusters, p_vals, _ = permutation_cluster_1samp_test(
    data_flat, adjacency=adjacency, n_permutations=1000,
    threshold=None, tail=0, out_type='mask', n_jobs=1)

# Summarize clusters
t_axis = np.arange(-pre_t, post_t, 1/sfreq)
signif = [(mask, p) for mask, p in zip(clusters, p_vals) if p <= 0.05]
print("Significant clusters (p<=0.05):")
if signif:
    for i, (mask, p) in enumerate(signif, 1):
        idxs = np.where(mask.flatten())[0]
        chs = np.unique(idxs // n_t)
        ts  = np.unique(idxs % n_t)
        print(f" Cluster {i}: p={p:.3f}, channels={len(chs)}, time {t_axis[ts].min():.3f}-{t_axis[ts].max():.3f}s")
else:
    print(" None")

# Channel-wise t-tests in 0.05-0.2s window
win_idx = np.where((t_axis >= 0.05) & (t_axis <= 0.2))[0]
mean_init = evokeds_init[:, :, win_idx].mean(axis=2)
mean_med  = evokeds_med[:, :,  win_idx].mean(axis=2)
t_vals = np.zeros(n_ch)
p_vals = np.ones(n_ch)
eff_sz = np.zeros(n_ch)
for ch in range(n_ch):
    t, p = stats.ttest_rel(mean_init[:, ch], mean_med[:, ch])
    d = (mean_init[:, ch] - mean_med[:, ch]).mean() / (mean_init[:, ch] - mean_med[:, ch]).std(ddof=1)
    t_vals[ch], p_vals[ch], eff_sz[ch] = t, p, d
sig_ch = np.sum(p_vals < 0.05)
print(f"Channels with uncorrected p<0.05: {sig_ch}/{n_ch}")

# Plot evoked waveforms
ga_init = evokeds_init.mean(axis=0).mean(axis=0)
ga_med  = evokeds_med.mean(axis=0).mean(axis=0)
plt.figure(figsize=(8,4))
plt.plot(t_axis, ga_init*1e12, label='Sentence-initial')
plt.plot(t_axis, ga_med*1e12, label='Sentence-medial')
plt.axvline(0, color='k', linestyle='--')
for mask, _ in signif:
    m = mask.reshape(n_ch, n_t)
    span = np.any(m, axis=0)
    if span.any():
        plt.axvspan(t_axis[span].min(), t_axis[span].max(), color='red', alpha=0.3)
plt.xlabel('Time (s)')
plt.ylabel('Amplitude (fT)')
plt.title('Magnetometer Evoked Responses')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

untried_experiments.hypothesis: During silence segments, gradiometer channels show higher relative power in the alpha band (8–13 Hz) than magnetometer channels.

experiment_plan.objective: Compare resting‐state alpha‐band power between gradiometer and magnetometer sensor groups during silence.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. For sessions 1–7, load each MEG HDF5 and its events TSV.
2. From the events table select all rows where kind=='silence'.
3. For each silence onset (timemeg), extract a 1 s continuous MEG epoch (0 to +1 s) from the raw data for both mag and grad channels; discard epochs that extend beyond recording boundaries.
4. For each epoch and each sensor group, compute the power spectral density (e.g., using Welch’s method) and average the PSD values in the 8–13 Hz band.
5. Within each session and sensor group, average alpha-band power across epochs.
6. Across sessions, perform a paired t-test comparing mean alpha power in grad vs mag groups.
7. Plot the grand-average PSD curves for both groups and mark the alpha band.
8. Report topographical maps of the alpha-band power difference across sensors.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
1. Grand‐average PSD plots (1–40 Hz) for grad and mag channels.
2. Sensor‐wise topographical maps of alpha power difference (grad–mag).
3. Paired t‐test statistics (t, p) comparing alpha power between sensor types.
4. Summary table of session-wise alpha‐band power values.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Word duration positively correlates with the duration of sustained MEG response (200–400 ms) in magnetometer channels.

experiment_plan.objective: Assess whether longer spoken words elicit more prolonged magnetometer activity in the 200–400 ms post-onset window.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. For sessions 1–7, load MEG and word‐level events.
2. For each word event, record its duration value and extract an epoch from –0.1 to +0.6 s in mag channels; baseline correct using –0.1 to 0 s.
3. For each epoch and channel compute the area under the absolute amplitude curve (AUC) in the 0.2–0.4 s window.
4. Pool (duration, AUC) pairs across all words in each session.
5. Within each session and channel, compute Pearson correlation between word duration and AUC.
6. Across sessions, average correlation coefficients and test whether mean correlation is significantly greater than zero (one‐sample t-test).
7. Plot scatterplots and regression lines for representative channels.

1. Session and channel‐wise correlation coefficients and p‐values.
2. Aggregate statistics (mean r, 95% CI) across sessions.
3. Example scatterplots of word duration vs MEG AUC.
4. Heatmap of correlation coefficients across sensors.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: The spatial pattern (topography) of sentence‐initial word evoked responses is highly consistent across sessions, as measured by the correlation of channel amplitudes at peak latency.

experiment_plan.objective: Quantify the consistency of initial‐word evoked topographies across the 10 recording sessions.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. For sessions 1–10, extract sentence‐initial word evoked responses in mag and grad channels (–0.1 to +0.4 s epochs, baseline corrected).
2. For each session, compute the mean evoked waveform (averaged across channels) and identify its global peak latency in 0.05–0.2 s.
3. At that latency sample, record the sensor‐wise amplitude vector (n_channels).
4. Compute Pearson correlation coefficients between every pair of sessions’ topography vectors.
5. Collect the distribution of inter‐session correlations; test whether the mean correlation is significantly above zero by a one‐sample t-test.
6. Visualize the session×session correlation matrix as a heatmap.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
1. Session‐wise peak latencies and topography vectors.
2. Correlation matrix of topographies across sessions.
3. Mean and confidence interval of inter‐session correlations.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Functional connectivity (pairwise correlation) between magnetometer channels increases in the 0–0.5 s window following word onsets compared to the ‑0.5–0 s baseline window.

experiment_plan.objective: Determine whether word processing transiently increases sensor‐level connectivity in the magnetometer array.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. For sessions 1–7, load MEG and word events.
2. For each word onset, extract two 0.5 s epochs: pre-onset (–0.5 to 0 s) and post-onset (0 to +0.5 s) from mag channels; baseline correct each epoch.
3. For each epoch compute the channel×channel Pearson correlation matrix.
4. Average correlation matrices across word events separately for pre and post periods within each session.
5. For each channel pair, compute the difference (post–pre) and perform a paired t-test across sessions.
6. Correct for multiple comparisons (e.g., FDR) to identify significantly strengthened connections.
7. Visualize the average connectivity matrices and the network of edges showing significant increase.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
1. Grand-average pre and post connectivity matrices.
2. List of channel pairs with significant connectivity increases (t, p corrected).
3. Network plot of significant edges over sensor layout.
4. Summary of connectivity change statistics.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Baseline MEG amplitude drifts linearly over each recording session, producing a measurable low‐frequency (<0.1 Hz) power increase across time bins.

experiment_plan.objective: Quantify slow baseline drifts in MEG channels over the course of each session.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. For sessions 1–10, load continuous magnetometer data and times.
2. Divide each session’s continuous recording into consecutive non‐overlapping 60 s bins.
3. For each bin and channel, bandpass‐filter the data between 0.01–0.1 Hz and compute the RMS amplitude (or mean absolute amplitude) as a proxy for low‐frequency power.
4. For each channel and session, fit a linear regression of RMS vs. time‐bin index; record slope.
5. Across sessions, assess whether the mean slope across channels is significantly positive (one‐sample t-test).
6. Plot example drift curves and the distribution of slope coefficients across channels.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
1. Per-channel slope values of low-frequency drift for each session.
2. Mean slope and 95% CI across channels and sessions.
3. Plots of low-frequency RMS amplitude vs. time bins for representative channels.
4. Histogram of drift slopes across channels.

    baseline_idx = t_axis < 0

        evoked2_list.append(epochs2.mean(axis=0))

ev2 = evoked2.mean(axis=0).mean(axis=0)

plt.ylabel('Amplitude (fT)')

plt.axvline(0, color='k', linestyle='--')
# Shade significant time windows
for cl in signif_clusters:

    t_idxs = np.unique(idxs % n_t)
    t0, t1 = t_axis[t_idxs].min(), t_axis[t_idxs].max()
    plt.axvspan(t0, t1, color='red', alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Print basic stats of t-tests per channel
sig_ch = np.sum(p_vals < 0.05)

{"code":"import h5py
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats, sparse
from mne.stats import permutation_cluster_1samp_test, combine_adjacency

# Parameters
sessions = range(1, 11)
pre_t, post_t = 0.1, 0.4  # seconds
np.random.seed(42)
evokeds_init, evokeds_med = [], []

# Loop over sessions
for sess in sessions:
    # Load MEG data
    with h5py.File(f'sub-0_ses-{sess}_meg.h5', 'r') as f:
        data = f['data'][:]            # (306, n_times)
        times = f['times'][:]
        sfreq = f.attrs['sample_frequency']
        ch_types = f.attrs['channel_types']
        if isinstance(ch_types, (bytes, bytearray)):
            ch_types = ch_types.decode('utf-8')
        ch_types = [c.strip() for c in ch_types.split(',')]
    mag_idx = [i for i, t in enumerate(ch_types) if t == 'mag']

    # Epoch parameters
    pre_samp = int(pre_t * sfreq)
    post_samp = int(post_t * sfreq)
    n_times = pre_samp + post_samp

    # Load events
    ev = pd.read_csv(f'sub-0_ses-{sess}_events.tsv', sep='\t')
    words = ev[ev.kind == 'word']
    init = words[words.sentenceidx == 1]
    med = words[words.sentenceidx > 1]

    # Extract epochs
    def extract(onsets):
        ep = []
        for t0 in onsets:
            idx = np.searchsorted(times, t0)
            i0, i1 = idx - pre_samp, idx + post_samp
            if i0 >= 0 and i1 <= data.shape[1]:
                ep.append(data[mag_idx, i0:i1])
        return np.array(ep)  # (n_epochs, n_ch, n_times)

    ep_init = extract(init.timemeg)
    ep_med = extract(med.timemeg)
    if ep_init.size and ep_med.size:
        # Baseline correction
        t_axis = np.arange(-pre_samp, post_samp) / sfreq
        base = ep_init[:, :, t_axis < 0].mean(axis=2, keepdims=True)
        ep_init -= base
        base = ep_med[:, :, t_axis < 0].mean(axis=2, keepdims=True)
        ep_med -= base
        # Session evoked
        evokeds_init.append(ep_init.mean(axis=0))
        evokeds_med.append(ep_med.mean(axis=0))

# Stack sessions: shape (n_sess, n_ch, n_times)
evokeds_init = np.stack(evokeds_init, axis=0)
evokeds_med  = np.stack(evokeds_med,  axis=0)
n_sess, n_ch, n_t = evokeds_init.shape

# Compute difference
diff = evokeds_init - evokeds_med  # (n_sess, n_ch, n_t)

# Build spatio-temporal adjacency
# Channel adjacency: identity (clusters only within same channel)
ch_adj = sparse.identity(n_ch, format='csr')
# Time adjacency: connect each time point to its neighbors
i = np.arange(n_t - 1)
j = i + 1
data_vals = np.ones(len(i))
rows = np.concatenate([i, j])
cols = np.concatenate([j, i])
time_adj = sparse.csr_matrix((np.concatenate([data_vals, data_vals]), (rows, cols)), shape=(n_t, n_t))
# Combine
connectivity = combine_adjacency(ch_adj, time_adj)

# Run cluster test
X = diff.reshape(n_sess, n_ch * n_t)
T_obs, clusters, p_vals, _ = permutation_cluster_1samp_test(
    X, connectivity=connectivity, n_permutations=1000,
    tail=0, threshold=None, out_type='mask', n_jobs=1)
# Extract significant clusters
signif = [(clus, p) for clus, p in zip(clusters, p_vals) if p <= 0.05]

# Print cluster summary
t_axis = np.arange(-pre_samp, post_samp) / sfreq
print("Significant clusters (p<=0.05):")
if signif:
    for idx, (mask, p) in enumerate(signif, 1):
        inds = np.where(mask.flatten())[0]
        chs = np.unique(inds // n_t)
        ts  = np.unique(inds % n_t)
        print(f" Cluster {idx}: p={p:.3f}, channels={len(chs)}, time {t_axis[ts].min():.3f}-{t_axis[ts].max():.3f}s")
else:
    print(" None")

# Channel-wise t-tests in 0.05–0.2s window
time_idx = np.where((t_axis >= 0.05) & (t_axis <= 0.2))[0]
mean_init = evokeds_init[:, :, time_idx].mean(axis=2)
mean_med  = evokeds_med[:, :,  time_idx].mean(axis=2)
t_vals = np.zeros(n_ch)
p_vals = np.ones(n_ch)
eff_sz = np.zeros(n_ch)
for ch in range(n_ch):
    t, p = stats.ttest_rel(mean_init[:, ch], mean_med[:, ch])
    d = (mean_init[:, ch] - mean_med[:, ch]).mean() / (mean_init[:, ch] - mean_med[:, ch]).std(ddof=1)
    t_vals[ch], p_vals[ch], eff_sz[ch] = t, p, d
sig_ch = np.sum(p_vals < 0.05)
print(f"Channels with uncorrected p<0.05: {sig_ch}/{n_ch}")

# Plot grand-average evoked
ga_init = evokeds_init.mean(axis=0).mean(axis=0)
ga_med  = evokeds_med.mean(axis=0).mean(axis=0)
plt.figure(figsize=(8,4))
plt.plot(t_axis, ga_init*1e12, label='Sentence-initial')
plt.plot(t_axis, ga_med*1e12, label='Sentence-medial')
plt.axvline(0, color='k', linestyle='--')
# Highlight significant time spans
for mask, _ in signif:
    m = mask.reshape(n_ch, n_t)
    span = np.any(m, axis=0)
    times_sig = t_axis[span]
    if times_sig.size:
        plt.axvspan(times_sig.min(), times_sig.max(), color='red', alpha=0.3)
plt.xlabel('Time (s)')
plt.ylabel('Amplitude (fT)')
plt.title('Magnetometer Evoked Responses')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

eff_sz = np.zeros(n_ch)
for ch in range(n_ch):
    t, p = stats.ttest_rel(mean_init[:, ch], mean_med[:, ch])
    d = (mean_init[:, ch] - mean_med[:, ch]).mean() / (mean_init[:, ch] - mean_med[:, ch]).std(ddof=1)
    t_vals[ch], p_vals[ch], eff_sz[ch] = t, p, d
sig_ch = np.sum(p_vals < 0.05)
print(f"Channels with uncorrected p<0.05: {sig_ch}/{n_ch}")

# Plot evoked waveforms
ga_init = evokeds_init.mean(axis=0).mean(axis=0)
ga_med  = evokeds_med.mean(axis=0).mean(axis=0)
plt.figure(figsize=(8,4))
plt.plot(t_axis, ga_init*1e12, label='Sentence-initial')
plt.plot(t_axis, ga_med*1e12, label='Sentence-medial')
plt.axvline(0, color='k', linestyle='--')
for mask, _ in signif:
    m = mask.reshape(n_ch, n_t)
    span = np.any(m, axis=0)
    if span.any():
        plt.axvspan(t_axis[span].min(), t_axis[span].max(), color='red', alpha=0.3)
plt.xlabel('Time (s)')
plt.ylabel('Amplitude (fT)')
plt.title('Magnetometer Evoked Responses')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()"}
